RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Wednesday, the December 18, 2002/Agrahayana 27, 1924 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Coal and Mines; Defence; Home Affairs; Non-Conventional
Energy Sources; Power; Rural Development; Textiles)
Total number of questions—20
121
Ash emitted by Thermal Power
Stations
†*401. SHRI P. K. MAHESHWARI:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the likelihood of change in
local ecology due to the ash emitted by
thermal power stations in the country;
(b) if so, the quantity of ash emitted by
each Thermal Power Station in the country
at present;
(c) the manner in which the ash is being
disposed off by these Thermal Power
Stations; and
(d) the manner in which Government
propose to deal with the hazards arising from
this ash?
Tax waiver policy for Naphtha-based
power projects
*402. SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to extend the tax waiver policy, available to
upcoming private power projects to
Naphtha-based power projects, some of the
State-run units and also to NTPCs five
Naphtha-based combine cycle plants;
(b) whether this exemption will bring
the public sector units at par with the private
power plants as far as tax obligations are
concerned; and
(c) if so, to what extent it has been helpful
for the State-run units?
Use of non-conventional energy
sources
*403. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of NON-
CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the use of
solar and other non-conventional sources
of energy have not gained momentum in the
country;
(b) the kind of non-conventional energy
produced from different sources during the
years 2000, 2001 and 2002;
(c) whether any industry or purpose has
been reserved for exclusive use of non-
conventional energy;
(d) if so, the details thereof;

(f) the steps being taken to maximize the
use of non-conventional energy sources?
Employment provided under SGRY
*404. SHRI RAMACHANDRA
KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details of additional employment
provided under Sampoorna Gramin Rojgar
Yojana, so far, in Orissa;
(b) whether Government have set up any
machinery for monitoring the
implementation of Sampoorna Gramin
Rojgar Yojana;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Rural electrification in Orissa
*405. SHRI SURENDRA LATH: Will
the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) the amount spent by the Rural
Electrification Corporation for providing
electricity to the villages in Orissa, during
Ninth Five Year Plan;
(b) the number of villages in that State
which have been electrified during that plan
period year-wise; and
(c) the reasons for tardy progress in rural
electrification in that State?
Parvathy Mill at Kollam in Kerala
*406. SHRI J. CHITHARANJAN:
SHRI V. V. RAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of TEXTILES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that the Parvathy Mill at Kollam in
Kerala, a mill run by the NTC, is not
functioning due to dearth of raw materials;
(b) the steps taken to improve the
functioning of the Mill; and
(c) whether Government propose to run
the Parvathy Mill as an independent Unit
under the NTC?
Policy on closure of abandoned mines
*407. SHRI ABANI ROY: Will the
Minister of COAL AND MINES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government had set up a
Committee to suggest changes in the policy
regarding closure of abandoned mines in
the country, in the recent past;
(b) if so, the details of recommendations
made by the Committee;
(c) whether Government have taken any
action on those recommendations; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Sick mills of NTC
*408. SHRI R. KAMARAJ: Will the
Minister of TEXTILES be pleased to state:
(a) the present condition of 119 sick mills
of National Textile Corporation, which have
been identified and promised to be developed
by special project announced by the
Ministry; and
(b) the funds provided for the
development of sick mills, State-wise?
Coal mafia in Chhattisgarh
†*409. SHRI JHUMUK LAL
BHENDIA: Will the Minister of COAL
AND MINES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
a gang of coal mafia is involved in

619
Phasing out manual jobs in
underground mines
2824. SHRI ABANI ROY: Will the
Minister of COAL AND MINES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Coal India Limited plans to
phase out manual jobs in underground
mining to raise productivity through
mechanisation;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether underground coal mining
through manual systems have been proved
to be risky and expensive; and
(d) if so, by when underground coal
mining through manual system is likely to
be abolished?
Foreign collaboration for the
development of mines
†2825. SHRI DILIP SINGH JUDEV:
Will the Minister of COAL AND MINES
be pleased to state:
(a) the countries with whom agreements
have been entered into for collaboration in
mining works;
(b) the details thereof;
(c) the details of benefits to the country
out of these agreements; and
(d) the details of cooperation in mining,
India has with other countries?
Mineral exploration by MECL in AP
2826. DR. DASARI NARAYANA
RAO: Will the Minister of COAL AND
MINES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Mineral Exploration
Corporation Limited (MECL) is conducting
mineral exploration activities in Andhra
Pradesh;
(b) if so, the details of the MECLs
activities in the State for the last three years;
(c) whether mineral deposits were found
in the State during the said period; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Forest degradation by mining
operations in Orissa
2827. SHRI SURENDRA LATH: Will
the Minister of COAL AND MINES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the large scale degradation of forests by the
mining operations in Orissa;

(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the guidelines sent to the mine owners
to stop any further degradation; and
(d) the steps taken to restore the ecology
in the mining area by each mine owners?
Production by Coal India Ltd.
†2828. SHRI DILIP SINGH JUDEV:
Will the Minister of COAL AND MINES
be pleased to state:
(a) the mechanism for the assessment of
the quantum of coal being produced by the
Coal India Ltd.;
(b) the quantum of coal produced by
each company during 2000-2001 and
2001-2002;
(c) the dates when the verification of the
same was carried out; and
(d) the company-wise details of the
shortage or surplus found in the said
verification?
Allotment of Captive Coal Block to
Karnataka
2829. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of COAL
AND MINES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government of Karnataka
has requested for allotment of Captive Coal
Block; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and
Government's reaction thereto?
Illegal mining and theft of coal
2830. DR. DASARI NARAYANA
RAO: Will the Minister of COAL AND
MINES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that despite the
contrary claims of CIL and its subsidiaries
illegal mining and theft of coal in the Coal
Mines continues unabated;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what remedial measures Government
have taken or proposed to take in this regard?
Import of coal
2831. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of COAL AND MINES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether coal is imported, if so, the
names of those countries with details of
imports over the last two years;
(b) how far it is cost-effective and more
useful to our consumers; and
(c) whether it has any effect on home
market, if so, the over-riding compulsions
to import?
Exploration of methane gas
2832. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of COAL AND MINES be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of coal mines identified,
till date, for the exploration of methane gas;
(b) the private companies going to be
involved in the exploration;
(c) the amount of money already invested
in the process; and
(d) by when the exploration of methane
gas is planned to begin in the country?
Expenditure by the officials of CIL on
foreign travel
2833. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA
MURTHY: Will the Minister of COAL
AND MINES be pleased to state:
(a) whether expenditure by the officials

on foreign travel during the year 2000-2001
has come under severe censure by the

CAG in this regard; and
(c) what is the extent of loss to the

Revision of coal royalty within a time
frame
